$comment: CR-W (protocol.md §11.50, ADOPTED at empyrean 265efaa7) wire vectors for emulator/screen_text's `panel` kind. ELEVEN cases: five `expect: pass` and six `expect: fail`. PROVENANCE: cases 1-4 are REAL REPLIES captured from oracle-player's own emulator/screen_text through Bus::call (the ignored test panel_attribution::tests::capture_cr_w_vector_replies, oracle 95bf549: a Loop bound to a private socket, a real NDJSON client, initialize, then the read - so each carries the D11 stamp the serving path adds), replacing the hand-built documents this file shipped while the kind was unserved - CR-H's bar, met. Case 5 is CR-H's live refusal capture, unchanged. Cases 6-11 are the declared-failure half and are hand-built by construction: they are documents a well-meaning implementer would produce and the fragment must refuse. RIDER R1's FIVE initialize CASES (the file's 12-16, 0-indexed 11-15) WERE DROPPED at the landing, not lost: R1 (initialize.capabilities.screenTextKinds) was DROPPED by the ruling, and §11.50 records that its three DECLARED-FAILURE cases do not go red against the schema as landed, because initialize.capabilities is not a closed object, so an unknown key passes. A fail-vector the schema cannot refuse is coverage theatre, and shipping it would report a green a reader takes for coverage. RESIDUE a document schema cannot see, all SERVER BEHAVIOUR and all conformance rows in the CR (section 9, W1-W10), each now tested in oracle: that a panel surface exists exactly when its body was drawn (W1), that the name is its tab title (W2), that `text` and `rendered` share joins at the same run boundaries (W3), that an unclipped unelided run has rendered == text (W4), that elision is read from the toolkit's own Galley::elided (W5), clipping (W6), hollow boxes (W7), and the blank panel (W8). RUN: crates/oracle-aether/tests/screen_text.rs::the_cr_w_vectors_validate_the_way_the_file_says_they_do judges every case here against the VENDORED fragment with the suite's own check_incoming_strict, keyed by method AND kind (a harness that ignores either measures the wrong fragment, which is the instrument note §11.50 records).

cases.why: [CR-W core] §11.50 - THE POPULATED REPLY, and it is a REAL one: captured from `oracle-player`'s own `emulator/screen_text` through `Bus::call`, by the ignored test `panel_attribution::tests::capture_cr_w_vector_replies` at oracle 95bf549 (the re-vendor commit), schema empyrean 265efaa7. Two leaves of the default dock are expanded and two collapsed, so two panel bodies were drawn this present and each is one surface named by its tab title; the hidden tabs sharing those leaves are absent because their bodies did not run (egui_dock-0.21.1 leaf.rs:1330). The Registers panel's `aether` row is CUT BY THE PANE EDGE: `rendered` stops at "...nothing can attach to this window" where `text` continues, so `truncated` derives true, and because both strings share their TAB/LF joins at the same run boundaries a client finds the cut run by comparing row for row. No elision mark on that run, because it was clipped rather than elided - the two cases the CR distinguishes, seen here in one reply.

cases.why: [CR-W core] §11.50 - A DRAWN PANEL WITH NO TEXT ON THE GLASS is PRESENT with empty strings, never omitted. REAL, captured from `--dock every-tab`'s arrangement at 1600x1000, where two bodies reach the blank case two different ways: Profiler paints no text shape at all, and Watchpoints paints text shapes with no glyph on the glass (an empty text shape is not a run, §11.50). Per-panel granularity is chosen over per-line surfaces for exactly this case: 'the panel is on screen and says nothing' and 'the panel is not on screen' must not be the same artifact.
